name: Inmon CIF (3NF EDW)
description: Bill Inmon's Corporate Information Factory builds the warehouse top-down: ETL cleanses and integrates every source into a subject-oriented, normalized (3NF) enterprise core — the single version of truth for the whole company — and departmental data marts are then derived from that core, never loaded directly from sources. The inverse of Kimball's mart-first approach: slower to first value, but the integrated core makes cross-domain consistency structural rather than aspirational. It remains the backbone pattern in banks, insurers, and other institutions where an authoritative, auditable enterprise model outweighs delivery speed.
when_to_use: Cross-domain consistency is the core requirement — finance, risk, and regulatory reporting must reconcile to one integrated model.
The organization is large and long-lived enough to amortize months of enterprise modeling before the first mart ships.
Auditability matters: regulators expect a documented, normalized system of record with controlled derivations.
Many marts will exist — deriving them from one core beats integrating the same sources repeatedly.
when_not_to_use: You need analytics in weeks — mart-first dimensional delivery (12) or an ELT stack (2) reaches value an order of magnitude faster.
Sources change frequently — every upstream change ripples through the normalized core and its derivations.
The team lacks dedicated data modelers; a 3NF enterprise model is a specialist discipline, not a side task.
Audit-heavy multi-source integration with more agility is the actual need — Data Vault (13) was designed as exactly that middle ground.

hot_spots.title: Delivery latency
hot_spots.detail: Months of enterprise modeling pass before the first mart ships, and sponsorship can die before value arrives.

hot_spots.title: Model rigidity
hot_spots.detail: Every source schema change ripples through the 3NF core and every dependent mart — change control becomes the bottleneck.

hot_spots.title: Mart drift
hot_spots.detail: Under deadline pressure, marts get loaded straight from sources, quietly breaking the single-version-of-truth guarantee.

hot_spots.title: Key management
hot_spots.detail: Enterprise-wide surrogate key pipelines are fragile; a key collision or late-arriving master record corrupts joins across subjects.

evolution.reason: Move the integration layer to Data Vault when source volatility makes the 3NF core too rigid.

stages.name: ETL
stages.role: Cleansing, conforming, and integrating sources before load
stages.rationale: CIF shops run on heavyweight ETL suites with metadata management and change control; Informatica remains the enterprise standard in this pattern.

stages.name: EDW core
stages.role: Subject-oriented normalized enterprise store — the single version of truth
stages.rationale: The modern build runs the 3NF core on a cloud warehouse; Teradata, Oracle, and Db2 are where most existing CIF estates live today.

stages.name: Dependent marts
stages.role: Dimensional derivations of the core per department
stages.rationale: Marts usually live as schemas in the same platform as the core — the discipline is that they derive from the core, never from sources.

stages.name: Metadata + governance
stages.role: The enterprise model, business glossary, and lineage that make the core authoritative
stages.rationale: CIF stands or falls on governed definitions; Collibra and Alation are the enterprise glossary/stewardship tools, DataHub the open alternative.

stages.name: BI + reporting
stages.role: Departmental reporting on marts, enterprise analysis on the core
stages.rationale: Standard enterprise BI over dependent marts; the guarantee that any two reports reconcile comes from the shared core, not the tool.
